title: Baseline reading comprehension
instructions: Read the passage and answer all five questions without hints or feedback.

parts.prompt: Why did the students swap the thermometers between huts?

options.text: To make the afternoon readings warmer
To prevent a fixed instrument difference being mistaken for a roof-colour effect
To measure roof colour directly
To reduce the number of readings

choice_rationales.B: The final paragraph states this control.

parts.hint: Protected baseline: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Swapping reduces instrument bias in the comparison.

parts.prompt: In the final paragraph, what does “Their method” refer to?

options.text: Asking the principal to choose a roof colour
Using similar huts, repeated timed readings and controls such as swapped thermometers
Painting every school building white
Comparing the huts only on cloudy afternoons

choice_rationales.A: The principal asks about one control but does not define the method.
choice_rationales.B: These linked design choices form the investigation method described throughout the passage.
choice_rationales.C: The team tested two huts and did not repaint school buildings.
choice_rationales.D: The readings covered ten days and several conditions.

parts.hint: Protected baseline: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Their method is the controlled, repeated comparison used to separate roof colour from other differences.

parts.prompt: What does “promising” most nearly mean in paragraph 3?

options.text: showing useful potential but not yet conclusive
guaranteed to work everywhere
too expensive to continue
unexpectedly dangerous

choice_rationales.A: Most readings favour white, but exceptions remain.

parts.hint: Protected baseline: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Promising signals encouraging but limited evidence.

parts.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea?

options.text: Dark roofs are always hotter than white roofs
Cloudy weather makes experiments impossible
School huts are identical to real classrooms
Careful controls and repeated measurements make a limited comparison more trustworthy

choice_rationales.A: The passage avoids an absolute claim.
choice_rationales.D: This joins the method, result and caution.

parts.hint: Protected baseline: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The investigation demonstrates how design quality supports a bounded conclusion.

options.text: The team expected every reading to be identical
The students valued a cautious conclusion more than an exaggerated result
The principal planned to repaint every classroom immediately
The dark roof was cooler on every cloudy day

choice_rationales.A: They were testing a possible difference.
choice_rationales.B: They explicitly avoided claiming the roof always worked.
choice_rationales.D: Only two cloudy afternoons are described as similar.

parts.hint: Protected baseline: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Their language and method show commitment to evidence boundaries.
